author: Ellen G. White
work: Letter 57, 1895 (to O. A. Olsen, May 1, 1895; printed as TM 91.2)
text: The Lord in His great mercy sent a most precious message to His people through Elders Waggoner and Jones. … Many had lost sight of Jesus. They needed to have their eyes directed to His divine person, His merits, and His changeless love for the human family. … It is the third angel’s message, which is to be proclaimed with a loud voice, and attended with the outpouring of His Spirit in a large measure.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Christ is pleading for the church in the heavenly courts above … that the world should no longer say, Seventh-day Adventists talk the law, the law, but do not preach or believe Christ.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Manuscript 24, 1888 (her account of the Minneapolis General Conference)
text: The third angel’s message is the proclamation of the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus Christ. The commandments of God have been proclaimed, but the faith of Jesus Christ has not been proclaimed by Seventh-day Adventists as of equal importance, the law and the gospel going hand in hand.

author: Ellen G. White
text: What constitutes the faith of Jesus that belongs to the third angel’s message? Jesus becoming our sin-bearer that He might become our sin-pardoning Saviour. He was treated as we deserve to be treated. He came to our world and took our sins that we might take His righteousness.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Righteousness is right doing

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: Since the law is the righteousness of God—a transcript of His character

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: the decalogue is a circle having a circumference as great as the universe and containing within it the moral duty of every creature.

author: Ellen G. White
text: They have sewed together fig leaves to cover the nakedness caused by transgression.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Review and Herald, March 8, 1881 (reprinted as FW 31.4)
text: God’s law is the mirror presenting a complete reflection of the man as he is

author: A. T. Jones
work: Lessons on Faith (compiled; first printed as an unsigned editorial in the Review and Herald while Jones edited it, December 27, 1898, p. 832)
text: He spoke the word only, and it was so. The word spoken, itself produced the thing.

author: A. T. Jones
work: Lessons on Faith (compiled; first printed as an unsigned editorial in the Review and Herald while Jones edited it, December 6, 1898, p. 782)
text: But when the Lord said, “I will come” and do it, the centurion checked Him, saying, “Speak the word only,” and it shall be done.

author: A. T. Jones
work: Lessons on Faith (compiled; first printed as an unsigned editorial in the Review and Herald while Jones edited it, December 27, 1898, p. 832)
text: Faith is the expecting the word of God to do what it says and the depending upon that word to do what it says.

author: A. T. Jones
work: Lessons on Faith (compiled; first printed as an unsigned editorial in the Review and Herald while Jones edited it, January 17, 1899, p. 40)
text: the same One who said, “Let there be light, and there was light,” … this same One speaks the righteousness of God unto and upon all that believe.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: The meaning of the word “justified” is “made righteous.” … But since all have sinned, there are none just or righteous before God; therefore they need to be justified, or made righteous, which God does.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimonies for the Church, vol. 5, “Joshua and the Angel”
text: He does not claim that Israel are free from fault. In his filthy garments, symbolizing the sins of the people, which he bears as their representative, he stands before the Angel

author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimonies for the Church, vol. 5, “Joshua and the Angel”
text: Then the Angel, who is Christ Himself, the Saviour of sinners, puts to silence the accuser of His people

author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimonies for the Church, vol. 5, “Joshua and the Angel” (first printed 1885 as T32 228.2)
text: Zechariah’s vision of Joshua and the Angel applies with peculiar force to the experience of God’s people in the closing up of the great day of atonement.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimonies for the Church, vol. 5, “Joshua and the Angel”
text: the command is given, “Take away the filthy garments” from them, and the encouraging words are spoken, “Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment.”

author: Ellen G. White
text: This robe, woven in the loom of heaven, has in it not one thread of human devising.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: Notice in the above account that the taking away of the filthy garments is the same as causing the iniquity to pass from the person. … when Christ covers us with the robe of His own righteousness, He does not furnish a cloak for sin but takes the sin away.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Through faith we receive the grace of God; but faith is not our Saviour. It earns nothing. It is the hand by which we lay hold upon Christ, and appropriate His merits, the remedy for sin.

author: Ellen G. White
text: The same Jesus has bidden me tell you, Look and live. Do not climb the pole, but only look. I present Christ to you. Look and live.

author: (unsigned; SDA Year Book 1889)
text: we are dependent on Christ, first, for justification from our past offenses, and, secondly, for grace whereby to render acceptable obedience to his holy law in time to come.

author: E. J. Waggoner
work: “Studies in the Book of Hebrews. - No. 16” (Sunday afternoon, Feb. 28, 1897), General Conference Daily Bulletin, March 8, 1897 (byline at page 297; the corpus author field names the editor, A. T. Jones)
text: for the Sabbath is righteousness by faith; for by it a man comes into God’s works, and those works are perfect. Therefore he gets rest by faith.

author: A. T. Jones
work: The Consecrated Way to Christian Perfection, ch. XVI “The Times of Refreshing”
text: we are in the times of refreshing—the time of the latter rain. … And the blotting out of sins is exactly this thing of the cleansing of the sanctuary

author: Ellen G. White
work: Review and Herald, June 24, 1884 (later GW92 414.2, 1SM 353.2 with added commas)
text: Repentance as well as forgiveness is the gift of God through Christ.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Faith earns nothing for us; it is the gift of God, which we may receive and cherish by making Christ our personal Saviour.

author: E. J. Waggoner
work: Studies in Romans, The Present Truth 10 (byline E. J. Waggoner; reprinted SITI March 12, 1896, 165.2 and WOR 94.2)
text: People are not simply counted righteous, but actually made righteous, by the obedience of Christ, who is as righteous as He ever was, and who lives today in those who yield to Him.

author: A. T. Jones
work: Lessons on Faith (compiled; first printed as an unsigned editorial in the Review and Herald while Jones edited it, January 1899)
text: In man’s life there is no righteousness. … The word of God received by faith—that is, the word of God expected to do what that word says and depended upon to do what it says—produces righteousness in the man and in the life where there never was any before

author: A. T. Jones
work: Lessons on Faith (compiled; Review and Herald, January 1899)
text: “Therefore being justified [made righteous] by faith [by ex-pecting and depending upon the word of God only] we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.”

author: Ellen G. White
work: Thoughts From the Mount of Blessing
text: God’s forgiveness is not merely a judicial act by which He sets us free from condemnation. It is not only forgiveness for sin, but reclaiming from sin. It is the outflow of redeeming love that transforms the heart.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: It is true that God will by no means clear the guilty. He could not do that and still be a just God. But He does something which is far better. He removes the guilt, so that the one formerly guilty does not need to be cleared—he is justified and counted as though he never had sinned.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: And this shows that the forgiveness of sins is something more than a mere form, something more than a mere entry in the books of record in heaven, to the effect that the sin has been canceled. The forgiveness of sins is a reality; it is something tangible, something that vitally affects the individual. It actually clears him from guilt, and if he is cleared from guilt, is justified, made righteous, he has certainly undergone a radical change.

author: E. J. Waggoner
work: “Our Inheritance”, The Present Truth 11, 19 (byline E. J. Waggoner)
text: Those who believe on the name of Christ have the privilege to become the sons of God. It is not simply the right to be called the sons, but the power actually to become sons.

author: Ellen G. White
text: There must be a power working from within, a new life from above, before men can be changed from sin to holiness. That power is Christ.

author: Ellen G. White
text: You cannot atone for your past sins; you cannot change your heart and make yourself holy. But God promises to do all this for you through Christ. … If you believe the promise,—believe that you are forgiven and cleansed,—God supplies the fact; you are made whole, just as Christ gave the paralytic power to walk when the man believed that he was healed.

author: Ellen G. White
text: The sinner could not be happy in God’s presence; he would shrink from the companionship of holy beings. Could he be permitted to enter heaven, it would have no joy for him. … It is no arbitrary decree on the part of God that excludes the wicked from heaven; they are shut out by their own unfitness for its companionship.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: The law of God is perfect righteousness, and perfect conformity to it is demanded of everyone who shall enter the kingdom of heaven.

author: Ellen G. White
text: God requires the entire surrender of the heart, before justification can take place; and in order for man to retain justification, there must be continual obedience, through active, living faith that works by love and purifies the soul.

author: Ellen G. White
text: You cannot change your heart, you cannot of yourself give to God its affections; but you can choose to serve Him. You can give Him your will; He will then work in you to will and to do according to His good pleasure.

author: Ellen G. White
text: thus through constant surrender to God you will be enabled to live the new life, even the life of faith.

author: Ellen G. White
text: God desires to heal us, to set us free. But since this requires an entire transformation, a renewing of our whole nature, we must yield ourselves wholly to Him.

author: Ellen G. White
text: This is a daily matter. Each morning consecrate yourself to God for that day.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Sanctification is not the work of a moment, but of a lifetime. It is not gained by a happy flight of feeling, but is the result of constantly dying to sin, and constantly believing and living to Christ

author: Ellen G. White
text: Sanctification is not the work of a moment, an hour, a day, but of a lifetime.

author: E. J. Waggoner
work: “The Witness of Faith”, The Present Truth 11, 12 (byline E. J. Waggoner)
text: We are made thus in Him by being created new, through the power of Him who is the Creator. Ephesians 2:10. Thus we are not simply “counted” righteous and perfect without being so, but are righteous in reality, by a new creation in Christ. God never deals with unrealities.

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: Christ says that he went justified; that is, made righteous.

author: A. T. Jones
work: The Consecrated Way to Christian Perfection, ch. XVI
text: it is the finishing of all transgression in our lives; it is the making an end of all sins in our character
